correctness.rationale: Under strict best-shot response, coexistence forces initially producing vertices to deactivate on first selection until extinction of one side; a uniform random first-update permutation proves the joint survivor probabilities. Independent Poisson update clocks give the harmonic commitment mean and memoryless postcommit completion mean, multiplied by total selection rate for discrete scheduled ticks. Explicit edge cases and geometrically dominated balanced asymptotics are established, and independent rational dynamic-programming recurrences agree for all 1936 tested small count states. Finite tests corroborate rather than prove the theorem.

value.rationale: The natural unresolved quantitative issue is which best-shot equilibrium random asynchronous play selects from an arbitrary initially active configuration, and how many random update opportunities it requires. The exact producer-ratio selection law, complete terminal-suffix spectrum, all-parameter mean and sharp N log N balanced clock provide structural decision and efficiency information not supplied by generic convergence or empty-start greedy-set results.
